# Environment assets: sources and licences

Every file in this folder comes from one of the two sources below. Nothing
here was generated by an AI image or 3D model service.

## `tps-demo/` — Godot "Third Person Shooter" demo (CC-BY 3.0)

- **Source:** https://github.com/godotengine/tps-demo, commit
  `a82f15448e9b015440d3bbdf5e10801b260c4e9f`.
- **Licence:** as stated in that repository's `LICENSE.md`:

  > All assets Copyright (c) 2018 Juan Linietsky, Fernando Miguel Calabró.
  > Distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License
  > version 3.0 (CC-BY 3.0) https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/legalcode
  >
  > Existing as derivatived work, many original Substance Painter materials
  > used to create this scene were kindly provided by GameTextures.com

- **Attribution:** "Container models and sci-fi panel textures by Juan
  Linietsky and Fernando Miguel Calabró (Godot TPS demo), CC-BY 3.0". The
  files have been modified, as listed below.

| File | Original | Modifications |
|---|---|---|
| `container_red.glb` | mesh `prop_container2` + doors from `level/geometry/models/props.glb`; maps `level/textures/props/container2_*` | Extracted the one prop from the level file and baked it to its own origin. Dropped the lightmap UV2 and vertex colours. Embedded the albedo, normal and ORM maps as JPEG, keeping 1024 px. Secondary material `tile_painted_gun_metal` maps resized to 512 px. 5,634 tris. |
| `container_teal.glb` | same mesh, maps `container1_*` (same UV layout) | As above. |
| `container_brown.glb` | mesh `prop_container4topbottom`; maps `container4_*` | As above, with alpha cutout (cutoff 0.98, as in Godot). 4,808 tris. |
| `tile_rivet_panels_*.jpg` | `level/textures/structure/tile_rivet_panels_*` | 2048 → 1024 px, PNG → JPEG. |
| `tile_painted_gun_metal_*.jpg` | `level/textures/structure/tile_painted_gun_metal_*` | 1024 → 512 px, PNG → JPEG. |
| `tile_anti_slip_*.jpg` | `level/textures/structure/tile_anti_slip_albedo`, `tile_anti_slip_metal_normal`, `tile_anti_slip_metal_orm` | PNG → JPEG. |

The ORM maps use the same channels as in Godot and glTF: R = ambient
occlusion, G = roughness, B = metalness. One exception is the `container3`
grey set, which Godot reads roughness from B; it is not shipped here, because
its UV layout does not match the closed container mesh.

## `ambientcg-rock020/` — ambientCG "Rock 020" (CC0 1.0)

- **Original asset:** ambientCG `Rock020`, 1K maps
  (`Rock020_1K_Color`, `_Normal`, `_Roughness`, `_AmbientOcclusion`).
  ambientCG publishes all of its assets under CC0 1.0 Universal (public
  domain); no attribution is required, but it is given here.
- **Obtained from:** ambientcg.com is blocked from the build environment. The
  files were taken from the pmndrs asset market mirror,
  https://github.com/pmndrs/market-assets (`files/materials/rock/`, commit
  `c9cfa0236a012093edd5affe200808752375bd90`). Its metadata credits
  `"creator": "ambientcg"`, and the original ambientCG file names are intact.
- **Modifications:**
  - colour and normal re-encoded as JPEG;
  - roughness (G) and AO (R) packed into `rock020_orm.jpg`.
- **Used for:**
  - boulders, sampled triplanar by `src/world/rocks.js`;
  - the ground's normal-map relief (`src/world/Environment.jsx`).

## Not from external sources

The boulder **shapes** are generated in code (`makeRockGeometry` in
`src/world/rocks.js`). The characters, habitats, walls, tower, sky and
effects are this project's own procedural models and materials.
